description:
Defect in fz-3ul.1 (5371db0a0), found by CI on PR #280: the lib test binary dies with SIGSEGV on Linux. Mechanism, measured: compiled code runs a delivered handler in the raising call's place (continue_after_raise tail-calls the handler from the frame that called the never-returning extern), so the frames between the try and the raise (the loop body, raise/2, panic/1) stay on the machine stack under the handler. A loop that raises and rescues every iteration (fixture 00720) grows the stack by those frames per iteration until a reduction yield unwinds it; with 4000 reductions per quantum that is hundreds of iterations of orphaned frames per quantum. On macOS aarch64 the test the_jit_delivers_every_raise_of_a_rescuing_loop_and_yields passes at the 2 MB default thread stack and overflows at RUST_MIN_STACK=524288; the receive-timeout control test passes at 262144. Linux frames are larger, so the default overflows there, as a plain SIGSEGV because the fault is in JIT frames.

Fix at the source, no second mechanism: a delivered raise unwinds like a yield and resumes like a yield, but inside the same quantum. fz_panic keeps delivering (pop handler, materialize the handler template over (kind, value, name)); the raising frame then returns 0 and every frame above unwinds to the quantum entry exactly as a yield does (the original approved design); the quantum loop, which both the JIT driver (src/exec/runtime.rs, after run_quantum) and the AOT driver (runtime/src/aot_shim.rs, after run_scheduler_closure) run, then resumes the delivered handler at once, without going back through the scheduler and without reset_reduction_budget, so the budget keeps flowing. The 'resume now or hand back to the scheduler' question is answered once, in one shared helper on Process used by both drivers; a delivered raise must be distinguishable from a reduction/explicit/GC-pressure yield by construction (either a dedicated slot for the delivered handler so runnable keeps meaning 'queued for the scheduler', or an exhaustive census of every path that sets runnable and returns 0 with a reason bit each), not by guesswork. fz_take_raised_handler and the in-place tail call go away; continue_after_raise after a never call becomes 'return 0, trapping only if the process neither failed nor has a delivered handler'. The interpreter path already unwinds its continuation Vec and is untouched except where the shared helper replaces duplicated checks. If a new slot holds the handler it is a GC root in Process::collect_garbage like the others.

Acceptance:
- A deterministic regression test in src/exec/runtime_test.rs runs fixture 00720 (100_000 raising iterations) and 00726 on the JIT on a std::thread::Builder thread with a 256 KiB stack and passes; the same test fails on 5371db0a0 (state the measured failure in the commit).
- 00720 still reports reduction_yields >= 1 on JIT and AOT and raises_delivered == 100000; the fz.runtime.raise event count is unchanged.
- fixtures 00709..00742 unchanged and green on interp, run and build.
- Unit test of the shared quantum-continue helper: a delivered handler continues the quantum; a reduction yield, an explicit yield, a park and a failure each hand back to the scheduler.
- .agent/docs/exceptions.md 'Reaching the handler' describes the as-built route (unwind to the quantum loop, resume in the same quantum) and runtime-telemetry.md stays true.
- Full gate green: RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo test --workspace --all-targets, doc tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt --check; and additionally RUST_TEST_THREADS=4 cargo test -p fz --lib green (CI's shape).
- No pin, golden or expected file of a pre-existing fixture changes.
title: A handled raise unwinds the machine stack before its handler runs, within the same quantum
